To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the voluntary disclosure on management's responsibility for financial reports is not an effective control tool to limit earnings management.
there is no evidence that the voluntary disclosure in Thailand of management's responsibility on the financial reports (i.e. the MRF) reduces earnings management.
the disclosure of an MRS is not an indicator of the quality of the financial reports.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the voluntary disclosure of the management responsibilities on the annual financial report.
the voluntary disclosure of an management's responsibility for financial reports (MFR) and earnings management in firms listed on Stock Exchange of Thailand.
the relationship between the voluntary disclosure of a MRF and earnings management, which is an important issue for investors, regulators, auditors, and other users of financial statements.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a voluntary disclosure of management’s responsibility on the financial report does not reduce the likelihood of earnings manipulation.
the MRF does not have a significant effect on earnings management.
the voluntary disclosure is not a sufficient tool to reduce earnings management.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
earnings management is not a problem of disclosure, it is an accounting problem.
a voluntary disclosure of an MRD does not guarantee earnings management.
the voluntary disclosure on the MRF is an ineffective tool for controlling the earnings management.
The main takeaway from our work is that
investors and regulators need to consider other factors in addition to the MRF when assessing a firm's earnings quality.
investors should be cautious in using the voluntary disclosure of an management's responsibility for financial reports as a tool to detect earnings management.
firms with or with an MRF manipulate their financial statements in a similar manner.
